patterns.consequences: We are able to represent data about tagging activities from web 2.0 applications, from document annotation projects, or from RDFa documents.

patterns.name: TaskExecution
patterns.intent: To represent actions through which tasks are executed.
patterns.competency_questions: which task is executed through this action? what actions can done in order to execute that task?
patterns.consequences: This CP allows designers to make assertions on roles played by agents without involving the agents that play that roles, and vice versa. It allows to express neither the context type in which tasks are defined, not the particular context in which the action is carried out. Moreover, it does not allow to express the time at which the task is executed through the action (for actions that do not solely execute that certain task).

patterns.name: Time indexed participation
patterns.intent: To represent participants in events at some time,To represent participants in parts of events.
patterns.competency_questions: When something participated in some event?; At what time an event had some participant?
patterns.solution: This pattern uses the Situation pattern to add temporal information to participation of objects into events.
patterns.consequences: We can represent participation relations with time. This enables participations at different times as well as partial participations in events.However, this pattern focuses on participation of one entity in one event. If complex events need to be represented (with subevents, more participants and times, etc.), a partonomic structure must be introduced, e.g. by creating a new pattern that composes TimeIndexedParticipation with PartOf.

patterns.name: Time indexed person role
patterns.intent: To represent classification of things at a certain time.
patterns.solution: This pattern is encoded by specializing the situation pattern and composing it with the agent role pattern.

patterns.name: time indexed part of
patterns.intent: To represent objects that have temporary parts.
patterns.competency_questions: When was this object part of this other one?; Which object was this one part of at a certain time?; What are the parts of this object at a certain time?
patterns.consequences: This Content OP allows designers to represent part-whole relations with a temporal index (holding at a certain time).

patterns.name: TimeIndexedSituation
patterns.intent: To represent time indexed situations.
patterns.competency_questions: At what time did a certain situation occur?; What situations occurred at a certain time?
patterns.solution: This pattern adds a time specification (the Time interval pattern) to the Situation pattern, in order to provide a handy solution to many cases.
patterns.consequences: We can represent situations that have an explicit time parameter.In principle, this can be done already with the Situation pattern, but this provides a handy composition with the TimeInterval pattern.

patterns.name: time interval
patterns.intent: To represent time intervals.
patterns.competency_questions: What is the end time of this interval?; What is the starting time of this interval?; What is the date of this time interval?
patterns.consequences: The dates of the time interval are not part of the domain of discourse, they are datatype values. If there is the need of reasoning about dates this Content OP should be used in composition with the region Content OP.

patterns.name: TimePeriod
patterns.intent: To represent time periods between events.
patterns.competency_questions: Which is the measurement unit of a time period?; Which is the value of a time period?
patterns.solution: A time period is modelled as a n-ary relation with a measurement unit and a numerical value.
patterns.consequences: The measurement unit and the numerical value of a time period (e.g. 1 year) can be modelled.

patterns.name: Topic
patterns.intent: To represent topics and their relations.
patterns.competency_questions: What is the topic of something?; What topics are included in this one?; What are the topics near to that one?
patterns.solution: Topics are modelled as conceptual complexes with part of (containment), overlap, and vicinity relations, and can be related to any kind of entity. They are disjoint from "Concepts", which can be at the "core" of topics.
patterns.consequences: We are able to represent topics, subjects, or themes of something, and to organize topics into partonomic and topological structures.In order to represent more sophisticated relations between topics, concepts, terms, etc., refer to the full ontopic.owl ontology.

patterns.name: Trajectory
patterns.intent: The pattern provides a model of trajectory, which is understood as a sequence of spatiotemporal points. The model generalizing the Semantic Trajectory pattern from [Hu, et al., COSIT 2013] by employing the notion of place, instead of location/geo-coordinate, to represent the spatial extent of the trajectory. This pattern is suitable for a variety of trajectory datasets and easily extendible by by aligning to or matching with existing trajectory ontologies, foundational ontologies, or other domain specific vocabularies.
patterns.competency_questions: Show the birds which stop at x and y; Show the birds which move at a ground speed of 0.4 m/s; Show the trajectories of rivers which cross national parks; Where are the ports at which the oceanographic cruise A3221 stopped after leaving Woods Hole?; List the places and times that represent the spatiotemporal extent of the 1990 World Chess Championship event
patterns.solution: This pattern is reengineered from [Hu, et al., COSIT 2013] with changes as described in the intent of the pattern.
patterns.consequences: Unlike the original version of Semantic Trajectory, this pattern omits the hook to the data source for fixes (which was a subclass of ssn:Device) because instead of location/geo-coordinate, the notion of place is employed to capture the spatial extent. Nevertheless, it should be relatively straightforward to extend this version if the user wishes to attach data source information to the fixes.

patterns.name: Transition
patterns.intent: To represent basic knowledge about transitions (events, states, processes, objects).
patterns.competency_questions: What states of some object are changed by what event during a transition?; What is the process that is invariant through the transition?; What transitions are occurring on what object at what time?
patterns.solution: This pattern composes the Time-indexed participation, Region, and Sequence patterns in order to represent changing of states for objects, fired by some event, through an underlying process.
patterns.consequences: We are able to represent part of the semantics involved in transitions (e.g. what is implied by Petri Nets): initial and final states, causal events, underlying processes, affected objects, and sequences of time intervals for situations and events.However, it is not possible to define axioms for automatically infer initial and final states from time sequences, because coreference is not allowed in OWL (not even in OWL2).

patterns.name: transportPattern
patterns.intent: The goal of the pattern is to facilitate modelling the movement of mass or energy from one location to another, based on a common persistent frame of reference.
patterns.competency_questions: What is the extent of a point source pollution event? Where was a package shipped from and where was it shipped to?
patterns.solution: The rive water was polluted from effluent near a large factory.A package left Auckland, New Zealand, at 5:45am on 01/06/2012 and arrived in Los Angeles, USA, on 01/12/2012.
patterns.consequences: This CP allows data modellers and ontology creators the ability to filter and categorise large geoscience data stores.

patterns.name: Types of entities
patterns.intent: To identify and categorize the most general types of things in the domain of discourse.
patterns.competency_questions: What kind of entity is that?; Is this an event or an object?; Is this an abstract value or a quality of an entity?
patterns.consequences: The type of any element of the knowledge base is always known.

patterns.name: VerticalDistribution
patterns.intent: The intent of the pattern is to be able to represent vertical distribution for aquatic resources.
patterns.competency_questions: What resource has what vertical distribution?
patterns.consequences: This pattern only allows to query what vertical distribution is typical of an aquatic resource. Whereas such values can be subject to observation, another pattern based on the generic 'observation' pattern should be used.The vertical distribution is intended to have a fixed set of values (to be defined as nominals) but this is not explicit in the pattern.

patterns.name: VesselSpecies
patterns.intent: to provide a direct relation between aquatic species and vessels that are able to catch them, regardless of the fishing gear used.
patterns.competency_questions: what vessel types can catch what species? (provided that species are caught by geartypes are used by vessel types)
patterns.consequences: This pattern should be used in scenarios where a VesselType can be deemed suitable for catching some AquaticSpecies for reasons other than mounting some fishing gear of a suitable GearType. It is strictly related to the gearspecies pattern, in that it uses the catchesSpecies and isCaught property pair to define this behaviour. For the sake of reuse, no domain is declared for catchesSpecies, appropriate restrictions having beed applied instead.

patterns.name: VesselWaterArea
patterns.intent: to represent a direct relation between vessel types and water areas regardless of what type of fishing gear is fitted
patterns.competency_questions: which vessel types can be used in which water areas?
patterns.consequences: The pattern can be used to represent a water area setting and the vessels that can be used there, no matter whether these constraints are legal or logistic. The hasWaterArea object property is used as in the gearwaterarea pattern. Usage of this property as applied to VesselTypes is related to, but not strictly dependent on the hasWaterArea property as applied to GearTypes.
